transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Well, honestly, what made me come in is that I keep getting up during long sales strategy meetings at work. I know I’m supposed to stay seated, but I just... I find myself getting up anyway, even if it’s just to refill my water or go pace by the printer. It's been happening enough that I felt like I needed to finally talk to someone about it.

Does this tendency to get up and pace happen only during these work meetings, or do you find yourself struggling to stay seated in other situations as well, like while watching a movie at home or sitting through dinner?

Um, I haven't really noticed it happening in other situations, to be honest. Like, if I'm at home watching a movie or sitting down for dinner, I'm usually fine staying put. It really just seems to be those long meetings at work where I... I just feel the need to get up and move around.
When you are in those meetings and feel the need to get up, what is going through your mind or how are you feeling emotionally in that moment?

I don't really know if anything specific is going through my mind. I'm just... bored, I guess? Or restless. I just feel this physical urge to stand up and stretch my legs. I don't feel anxious or upset or anything like that. I just feel like I've been sitting for too long and my body wants to move.
Outside of these meetings, do you find that you spend a significant amount of time worrying about various aspects of your life, such as your work performance, finances, or personal health?

No, not really. I mean, I have normal concerns like anyone else, but I wouldn't say I spend a lot of time stressing over my job or my health or anything like that. I'm usually pretty okay with all of that. It really is just the physical restlessness during those long meetings that's been bothering me.
In your day-to-day life, do you frequently find yourself struggling to stay organized, losing track of important tasks, or forgetting appointments?

Yeah, I actually do struggle with that a bit. Especially with work. My campaign notes always seem to end up split between emails, sticky notes, my planner, and just... random open tabs on my computer. Because it's all over the place, I end up wasting a lot of time just trying to figure out what to do first instead of actually just starting the work.
Looking back at your time in school, did you struggle with staying organized or sitting still in class, or is this something that only started recently?

No, it's definitely not a recent thing. I remember it starting way back, even before high school. My elementary school teachers would always write on my report cards that I was bright but that I rushed through things. They said I talked out of turn a lot and forgot my homework. And my desk... it was always just stuffed full of half-finished papers and a total mess. So yeah, it's been an issue for a long time.
In your daily life, do you often find yourself acting or speaking before you have had a chance to think about the consequences?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I know I can be pretty talkative, especially since I work in sales, but I don't usually just blurt things out or do things without thinking about it first. I feel like I have a decent filter. So, yeah, I haven't really noticed that being an issue for me.
Outside of those meetings, do you find yourself feeling a need to fidget, tap your feet, or move around frequently even when you are just sitting and relaxing at home?

Not really, no. When I'm just at home trying to relax, I don't really notice myself doing that. I can usually just sit on the couch and watch a show without feeling like I need to get up or bounce my leg or anything. So, no, I wouldn't say that's an issue for me.
When you are working on a task or project, do you often find it difficult to maintain your focus until the task is actually finished?

Yeah, I do. Um, especially in longer strategy meetings or when I'm trying to read through a client brief. I usually start out really focused, but... then after a few minutes, I'll realize I've just been staring at the exact same slide, or the same paragraph, and I have absolutely no idea what the last point even was. So, yeah, it's definitely hard for me to keep my attention on something all the way through to the end.
Do you find that you frequently interrupt others while they are speaking or find it difficult to wait for your turn in conversation?

Yeah, I do that sometimes. Like, if I'm at work and I think of an idea while someone else is presenting a deck or something, I'll just kind of pop over or interrupt their conversation to add my thought. I mean, looking back, it probably could have waited, but I just sort of jump in right then.
When you are performing tasks at work, do you often make careless mistakes or fail to pay close attention to details?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I try to be pretty thorough when I'm putting together proposals or reviewing contracts. I might miss a small typo here or there, but nothing major or careless. I usually double-check my work before sending it out.
In your day-to-day life, do you frequently lose items that are necessary for your work or daily tasks, such as your keys, wallet, phone, or specific work documents?

Yes, I definitely do. It feels like I’m constantly hunting for things I need for work. Um, I'll spend time looking for my headset, client one-pagers, my keys... or even just the notebook I was using, like, ten minutes earlier. I just set things down and then have absolutely no idea where they went.

Beyond interrupting others during conversations, do you often find that you struggle to wait your turn in other social or professional situations, such as waiting in lines or waiting for your turn to speak in group settings?

Yeah, definitely. When I'm on client calls or in office discussions, waiting for my turn to speak makes me really restless. I, um, I'll catch myself constantly checking the clock, or just sitting there rehearsing what I want to say over and over in my head. And then a lot of the time, I just end up blurting it out way too early because I feel like I can't hold onto it anymore.
